cur:catacombs2-balazuc-sarcophagus.summary: Seven niches crowned by alternating pediments and arches, separated by spiral columns, frame biblical scenes on this Arles-made sarcophagus found in the Ardèche. Christ raises Lazarus, heals the paralytic and a blind man and foretells Peter's denial, while at one end Job sits in conversation with his friends. The photograph shows it in 2022, when it was lent to the Lyon Biennale of contemporary art.
facts: It was discovered in the 16th century at Les Salles, in the commune of Balazuc (Ardèche), and long kept in the church of Saint-Maurice-d'Ardèche.
In 1851 it went to the Musée des Beaux-Arts in Lyon and later to the Gallo-Roman museum at Fourvière (now Lugdunum); a cast is shown in Balazuc town hall.
The scenes were identified by the abbé Joseph-Alexandre Martigny in a memoir published in 1864.

cur:objects-lyon-christ-pantocrator-ivor.summary: A half-length Christ fills this ivory plaque, his bearded face framed by long hair and a cross-nimbus, the abbreviation of his name carved on either side. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds against his chest a gospel book with a jewelled cover. The intense, frontal gaze is the image of the Pantocrator, the Ruler of All, that Byzantine artists placed in domes, on coins and on precious objects alike.
facts: The museum label identifies it as a Byzantine work of the late 10th or early 11th century, 12.9 cm high, inventory L 412.
The bust of Christ holding a book and blessing became, after the end of Iconoclasm in 843, the standard Byzantine image of Christ Pantocrator (type).
